claim_detail.claim: A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions
A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning

command_detail.name: start

moments.title: The strongest model, at maximum effort, renaming a variable
moments.description: Why effort and capability drift to maximum by default, and how named profiles make them a decision instead of a habit.
moments.hook: watched the strongest model, at maximum effort, rename a variable

claim_detail.claim: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes
A profile names a capability class rather than a vendor model
Escalating reasoning effort after repeated blocked attempts is recorded rather than assumed
A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more

command_detail.name: start
command_detail.summary: begin a scoped task under a profile

moments.title: Accepting "done" because the model said so
moments.description: Why a sentence is not a completion criterion, and how a finish contract with typed outcomes replaces it.
moments.hook: accepted "done" because the model said so, and paid for it the next morning

claim_detail.claim: finish evaluates the finish contract line by line and refuses when any line is unmet
An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
Every finding carries the command that reproduces it

command_detail.name: finish
command_detail.summary: evaluate the finish contract; refuse if unmet

moments.title: Two different rulebooks for one repository
moments.description: Why CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md drift apart, and how one policy generates every instruction file with its own stamp.
moments.hook: opened CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md and found two different rulebooks for one repository

claim_detail.claim: Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically
Every generated instruction file carries its own stamp, and a hand edit is detected
A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten
The always-loaded instruction file has a line budget with a failing check
Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs

command_detail.name: doctor
command_detail.summary: is Majordomus itself healthy and actually wired here?

moments.title: Re-arguing a decision that was settled last week
moments.description: Why a decision that lives only in a transcript is reopened by the next session, and how a recorded reason and an explicit open question replace the argument.
moments.hook: watched a session undo last week's decision, for the reason it was made

claim_detail.claim: A decision is recorded with its reason and its task, and is superseded by a later entry rather than edited
A decision record without a task, a head and a reason is reported, and does not block
An unresolved question blocks acceptance, and an entry the gate cannot parse is a failure rather than a silent pass
A blocking question keeps blocking after the work is handed to a new task
An entry in the questions store that does not parse blocks acceptance exactly as an unresolved question does

command_detail.name: question
command_detail.summary: open, resolve and list questions that block acceptance

moments.title: A task "in progress" that nobody has touched for three weeks
moments.description: Why an abandoned task looks active, and how computed identity, checkpoint intervals and drift reports tell a live task from a dead one.
moments.hook: found a task "in progress" that nobody had touched for three weeks

claim_detail.claim: Identity fields on every state record are computed from git and never authored
A task record names the checkout it belongs to, and another checkout is never held to its scope
A checkpoint is a capped progress record with computed identity, and a body over the cap is refused rather than truncated
A profile sets how often a worker should checkpoint, and a stale task is reported
check reports whether state, scope, blockers and checkpoint age are consistent right now
watch reports policy, projection, state, scope, handover, verification, staleness and retention drift

command_detail.name: checkpoint
command_detail.summary: record compact progress inside the active task

command_detail.name: watch
command_detail.summary: what has drifted: state, policy, projections, retention

moments.title: Asking what the workers did last night, and getting a transcript
moments.description: Why a conversation log cannot answer an operational question, and how an append-only ledger with a closed vocabulary can.
moments.hook: asked what the workers did last night and had only transcripts to grep

claim_detail.claim: The ledger is readable back as operational history, filtered by task, event and time
Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event, and a malformed line is a failure rather than a skipped record
The ledger's event vocabulary is closed, on the way in and on the way out
Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index
Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them
The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked
Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented

command_detail.name: search
command_detail.summary: find durable records without reading all of them

moments.title: The rule for that directory, in a README no session ever loaded
moments.description: Why one always-loaded file cannot carry every local rule, and how a tree of scoped documents is composed for the path a worker is about to touch.
moments.hook: found the rule for that directory in a README no session ever loaded

claim_detail.claim: The context that applies to a path is composed from the layer's scoped documents, root to target, in one deterministic order with provenance, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing

The impact of a change set on the scoped context is reported from git — the documents, the scopes below them, moves with their ancestry, tracked sources to review, and stale projections — and an unrelated change reports nothing
The repository's AI layer is one directory whose manifest names every section, readable without the tool
The assembled context obeys a line budget, and every section it drops is named with its reason
The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing
The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused

command_detail.name: context
command_detail.summary: what the next worker needs to know now, within budget

command_detail.name: rules
command_detail.summary: the effective rule set: vendored baseline plus project rules   (read-only, except vendor update)

moments.title: Three roadmaps, and none of them true
moments.description: Why a plan kept in prose disagrees with itself the first time anything changes, and how a dependency graph with derived status replaces it.
moments.hook: read three roadmaps for one project and believed none of them

claim_detail.claim: Milestones and issues are canonical repository files, and a key nobody reads is an error
Issue and milestone status is derived from recorded facts and is stored nowhere
A cycle, a self-dependency and a dependency on an issue that does not exist are each refused by name
Execution waves are computed from the graph, and issues in one wave that touch the same paths are reported as serialised
An issue cannot be completed while a required piece of evidence is missing
The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it
GitHub milestones and issues are generated from the canonical model, and a hand-edited generated region is reported rather than overwritten

command_detail.name: plan
command_detail.summary: the milestone and issue model: validate, read, and move an issue
